topic.title: Mostly paying interest on a UK credit card: when the rules make the card company step in

title: A £3,000 card on the minimum: when UK rules make the lender step in
description: £3,000 on a UK credit card at 1.8% a month, paying only a 3% minimum. Most of the first year goes on interest, and UK rules call this persistent debt: after a year and a half the card company must contact you, and after three years it must offer a way to clear it in a reasonable time. Free debt help: StepChange, National Debtline, Citizens Advice. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions. Illustrative only. Not financial advice.

lines.text: Pay only the minimum on a £3,000 card, starting at £90? That takes 23 years to clear.
In year one you pay £1,009. But £587 of that is just interest.
After all that, you still owe £2,578.
UK card rules have a name for this: persistent debt.
Pay more in interest and fees than off the balance for a year and a half, and the card company must contact you. After three years, it must offer a way to clear it.
And free debt charities can help you plan it.
So, how much of your card payment is just interest?

maths card (min_due_pct 2.5 at rate_pct_month 1.8): unrealistic for a UK card. UK minimums must cover at least interest, fees and charges plus 1% of the balance (2011 industry agreement, now FCA rules), i.e. at least 2.8% here; a 2.5% minimum barely exceeds the 1.8% interest, so the 36 years, £6,740 interest and year-one split all rest on a minimum no UK card sets. Use min_due_pct >= 2.8 (e.g. 3%: ~23 years, £1,009 paid in year one, £587 of it interest - still persistent debt) or phrase the minimum as interest + 1%.

hook beat 'Only ever pay the £75 minimum on a £3,000 card? That takes 36 years to clear.' (and screen 'Minimum due £75'): misleading. The minimum shrinks with the balance; paying a fixed £75 a month would clear it in about 6 years. Say the minimum is £75 at first and falls as the balance falls, or 'pay only the minimum each month'.

name beat screen line 'more interest than balance': wrong definition. Persistent debt (FCA CONC 6.7.27) is paying more in interest, fees and charges than you repay of the balance over 18 months, not interest exceeding the balance. Use e.g. 'more on interest than off the balance'.

Confirmed OK: rules beat (18 months -> firm must contact you; 36 months -> must offer a way to repay in a reasonable period) matches FCA press release fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/new-credit-card-rules-introduced-fca and FOS decisions citing CONC 6.7.27; ~21.6% APR realistic for UK; no lender named; charities named per verify list; description ends with disclaimer.
